input: Set up a home composting system

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the user has an outdoor garden, a balcony, or only indoor space completely changes which composting method is viable — e.g., outdoor bin vs. worm bin vs. bokashi.
The types of waste they want to compost (food scraps only, garden/yard waste, meat/dairy) determines the method, bin size, and setup complexity.
Budget affects whether they buy a ready-made bin, tumbler, or build a DIY solution, and what accessories they can include.
How much time and effort they are willing to invest in maintenance (turning, monitoring) determines which system suits them — passive vs. active composting.
Knowing who else is in the household (family, flatmates) matters for sizing the system and ensuring buy-in from others who will contribute waste.
What they plan to do with the finished compost — use it in a garden, give it away, reduce landfill waste — clarifies how much output they need and how fast.
Concerns about odour, pests, or aesthetics will strongly influence which system and location they choose, especially in shared or urban settings.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a home composting system
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a composting system at home to process organic waste into usable compost.

questions.title: Do you have outdoor space, a balcony, or only indoors?
questions.description: Identifies where the composting system will be physically located, which is the primary filter for choosing a method.

questions.title: What types of waste do you want to compost?
questions.description: Determines whether the system needs to handle just fruit/veg scraps, yard waste, cooked food, or all of the above.

questions.title: What is your budget for setting this up?
questions.description: Clarifies whether to recommend a DIY build, a basic bin, or a premium tumbler or electric composter.

questions.title: How much weekly maintenance time are you willing to spend?
questions.description: Distinguishes between low-effort passive systems and faster active systems that require regular turning and monitoring.

questions.title: How many people in your household will contribute to it?
questions.description: Determines the volume of input waste to size the system correctly.

questions.title: What do you plan to do with the finished compost?
questions.description: Shapes how much output is needed and how quickly, influencing the method and scale chosen.

questions.title: How important is avoiding odours or deterring pests to you?
questions.description: Identifies aesthetic and hygiene priorities that may rule out certain open-bin systems or dictate placement and enclosure choices.
